Academic-practice prompt starters (RTCF), categorised strand > graduate competency > pathway > tier from the universal benchmark keys, plus `activities`: one per pathway capability, each a sequence of prompts (explain, see an example, try it, check my attempt, evidence it) with {verb} and {topic} slots; verbs come from the voice specification section 16 band the pathway tier anchors to; and `pathwayPrompts`: one practical prompt per pathway, distilled by hand from its 9 capability statements, with a suggested role. Draft wording: review before release.

knowledge.label: Knowledge
format: Start with a plain-language summary, then give me three questions to check my understanding.

thinking.label: Thinking
format: Set it out as a table: claim, evidence, my judgement, and what would change my mind.

application.label: Application
format: Give me a worked example, then a similar task for me to try on my own.

communication.label: Communication
format: Show me a short model, then tell me two things to change in my own draft.

autonomy.label: Autonomy
format: End with one next step I can take on my own and how I will know it worked.

introductory.label: Introductory
context: Pitch your help for a learner who begins to apply the subject's basic methods to familiar, well-defined tasks with guidance, works with sources and data they are given, and communicates straightforward findings clearly.

intermediate.label: Intermediate
context: Pitch your help for a learner who applies the subject's methods to questions and problems, carries out supervised research and enquiry, works with data and sources, and communicates findings to different audiences.

advanced.label: Advanced
context: Pitch your help for a learner who designs and critiques enquiry across methods, evaluates evidence and arguments critically throughout, and applies knowledge to current and complex problems with some originality.

pathwayPrompts.title: Starting, Progressing and Succeeding
pathwayPrompts.prompt: I want to get more out of studying {topic} in [subject]. Help me work out what excelling would look like for me now: ask me three questions about how I study, then help me set one goal about mastering the material rather than just the mark, name one pressure that knocks my confidence and a way to manage it, and put one strength into words I could use with an employer. Treat my setbacks as part of learning. Coach me with questions; do not answer for me.

pathwayPrompts.title: Understanding Learning, Assessment and Feedback
pathwayPrompts.prompt: Here are the learning outcome, marking criteria and feedback for my work on {topic}: [paste them]. Help me read them as a tutor would: explain what the outcome asks me to show and whether the task is formative or summative, then help me judge my own work against the criteria, pick the two feedback points that matter most, and turn them into an action plan with one question to take to my tutor. Ask me to make each judgement before you give yours.

pathwayPrompts.title: Finding and Using Sources
pathwayPrompts.prompt: I need scholarly sources on {topic} for [subject]. Be my search partner, not my searcher: help me pull keywords and synonyms from my task, build one search string with Boolean operators for the library discovery service, and plan how I will refine it after the first results and extend it through citation searching. Then give me three questions to test each source for currency, authority and relevance, and tell me how I will know the main debates are covered. Do not list sources for me.

pathwayPrompts.title: Referencing, Citation and Academic Integrity
pathwayPrompts.prompt: Check my referencing on {topic} without rewriting my work. Here are a paragraph and its references in [referencing style]: [paste them]. Tell me where a quotation or paraphrase needs acknowledging, where an in-text citation or reference list entry is incomplete or inconsistent, and how to reference any trickier source types. Then ask me one question about why acknowledging this source matters for honest, fair work in my field.

pathwayPrompts.title: Criticality
pathwayPrompts.prompt: Help me think critically about {topic} in [subject] rather than describe it. First ask me to sum up the main positions in the debate and who holds them. Then, for one scholarly interpretation I give you, question me on its argument, evidence and method until I can say what it does well and where it is weak. Finally, push me to judge which factors matter most and to state my own position, and point out where my stance shapes my reading.

pathwayPrompts.title: Academic Writing
pathwayPrompts.prompt: I am writing an assignment on {topic} in [subject]: [paste the question and my draft]. Do not rewrite it. First help me check I have read the question's steer and keywords correctly. Then review the draft for structure, argument, clarity and use of sources: show me where a paragraph lacks a clear point, where a sentence would be clearer in the active voice, and where a source speaks before I do. Finish with the three edits that would most improve it and a proofreading checklist.

pathwayPrompts.title: Presenting
pathwayPrompts.prompt: I am giving a [time]-minute presentation on {topic} for [subject] to [audience]. Help me plan it from the brief: what it is testing, a clear structure with an engaging opening, and accessible slides that follow "less is more". Then rehearse with me: ask the three hardest questions an examiner or panel might ask, and give feedback on how clearly and confidently I defend my argument. If it is a group presentation, help us agree roles and how we will handle disagreement.

pathwayPrompts.title: Revising and Exams
pathwayPrompts.prompt: My [exam type] on {topic} is in [number] weeks. Help me revise actively, not by rereading: ask me questions to find the gaps in what I know, build a simple plan that targets them in the time I have, and suggest two active techniques to try. After each session, quiz me without notes so I can judge what is working and change my plan. Finish with a strategy for the day itself, including how to manage nerves.

pathwayPrompts.title: Researching and Research Methods
pathwayPrompts.prompt: I am planning a research project on {topic} in [subject]. Act like a supervisor who questions me rather than designs it for me. Help me narrow the topic to a question I can answer, with a rationale and aims; place it in the literature I have read so far; choose and justify a methodology and methods; spot the ethics issues, including consent and anonymity; and check that the scope fits my time and word count. End by naming the weakest part of my plan.

pathwayPrompts.title: Reflective Practice
pathwayPrompts.prompt: Help me reflect on a recent experience of {topic}: [describe what happened]. Take me through a reflective model one stage at a time, asking questions rather than writing it for me. Push me past description: what went well and what did not, why, and how my own values and assumptions shaped what I noticed. Finish by helping me turn it into a dated action plan I could use for my continuing professional development.

pathwayPrompts.title: Work-Based and Experiential Learning
pathwayPrompts.prompt: I am starting a placement or work experience in [setting], linked to {topic}. Help me get the most from it: set two learning goals, plan how to use my mentor or supervisor, and pick one theory from my course to test in practice. Afterwards, take me through Kolb's experiential learning cycle on one real situation, ask me to justify a professional judgement I made, and help me say what it taught me about the practitioner I am becoming.

pathwayPrompts.title: AI and Technology
pathwayPrompts.prompt: I want to use AI responsibly on my work on {topic} in [subject]. Before anything else, ask me what my module's assessment guidance allows. Then act as a critical friend, not a ghost writer: help me decide which parts of the task AI could support and which must be my own thinking, show me how to fact-check anything you tell me, and help me write an honest statement of how I used AI. Remind me that you are not a source I can cite.

pathwayPrompts.title: Creativity
pathwayPrompts.prompt: Help me take a more creative approach to {topic} in [subject]. Run a structured session: first help me generate as many ideas as I can without judging them, then help me choose between them using criteria I set. If I get stuck or slip into perfectionism, suggest a different method to try. Finally, help me turn the best idea into a small first step I can act on this week, and explain which creativity approach we used and why it suits the task.
